title: Boss: the rename that parked 14,000 orders
summary: An incident and its follow-ups: a schema diff, a deploy-order verdict, a Protobuf breaking-change check and a replay of the parked messages.

steps.title: INC-2290: shipping parked 14,212 orders after orders-api 3.4
body: **INC-2290 · Sev 2 · shipping** · post-incident actions assigned to you
`orders-api` 3.4 renamed `total` to `amount` "to match the API". The registry subject was in `NONE` mode, so the
new schema registered. `shipping-worker` failed every message for 47 minutes:
14:12:03 fail: Shipping.OrderPlacedHandler  KeyNotFoundException: The given key 'total' was not present
14:12:03 warn: Shipping.Consumer  record orders-2@551200 dead-lettered after 5 attempts to orders.dlq
1. CI prints a readable **schema diff** on every pull request that touches a contract.
2. CI states the **deploy order** a change needs, or that it needs a new event version.
3. The same gate for the team's **Protobuf** contracts: removed numbers must be `reserved`, numbers never change type.
4. **Replay** the parked messages through a tolerant, upcasting reader; anything still unreadable stays parked

steps.title: 1. A readable schema diff
prompt: Write `List<string> Diff(List<Field> oldSchema, List<Field> newSchema)` (the tests define
`record Field(string Name, string Type, bool HasDefault);`). Go through the **old** fields in order:
- missing from the new schema → `"removed {name}"`;
- type changed → `"changed {name}: {oldType} -> {newType}"`;
- otherwise, default dropped → `"dropped default on {name}"`, or default added → `"added default on {name}"`.
Then go through the **new** fields in order; each one not in the old schema →
`"added {name} (with default)"` or `"added {name} (required)"`.
An identical schema gives an empty list.
solution: else if (!o.HasDefault && n.HasDefault) changes.Add($"added default on {o.Name}");
foreach (var n in newSchema.Where(n => oldSchema.All(o => o.Name != n.Name)))
hints: Look each old field up by name in the new schema; an `if / else if` chain picks the one message.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoOld = new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false), new("total", "int", false), new("currency", "string", true) };
var dojoInc = new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false), new("amount", "int", false), new("currency", "string", true) };
Dojo.Eq("the INC-2290 rename", new List<string> { "removed total", "added amount (required)" }, Diff(dojoOld, dojoInc));
var dojoMixed = new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false), new("total", "long", false), new("currency", "string", false), new("giftWrap", "boolean", true) };
Dojo.Eq("type change, dropped default, optional add", new List<string> { "changed total: int -> long", "dropped default on currency", "added giftWrap (with default)" }, Diff(dojoOld, dojoMixed));
var dojoDefaulted = new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false), new("total", "int", true), new("currency", "string", true) };
Dojo.Eq("a default added", new List<string> { "added default on total" }, Diff(dojoOld, dojoDefaulted));
Dojo.Eq("no change", new List<string>(), Diff(dojoOld, dojoOld));
record Field(string Name, string Type, bool HasDefault);

steps.title: 2. Which side deploys first?
prompt: Write `string DeployOrder(List<Field> oldSchema, List<Field> newSchema)` using `CanRead` (already in the editor):
- `backward` = the new schema can read old data: `CanRead(newSchema, oldSchema)`;
- `forward` = the old schema can read new data: `CanRead(oldSchema, newSchema)`.
Return:
| backward | forward | result |
| yes | yes | `"any order"` |
| yes | no | `"consumers first"` |
| no | yes | `"producers first"` |
| no | no | `"breaking: publish a new event version"` |
starter: if (!r.HasDefault) return false;   // the reader needs a value the writer never wrote
return true;                               // writer fields the reader does not know are skipped
solution: if (!r.HasDefault) return false;   // the reader needs a value the writer never wrote
return true;                               // writer fields the reader does not know are skipped
hints: Compute both booleans, then a tuple `switch` on `(backward, forward)`.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoOld = new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false), new("total", "int", false) };
Dojo.Eq("optional field with a default", "any order", DeployOrder(dojoOld, new List<Field>(dojoOld) { new("currency", "string", true) }));
Dojo.Eq("remove a required field", "consumers first", DeployOrder(dojoOld, new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false) }));
Dojo.Eq("add a required field", "producers first", DeployOrder(dojoOld, new List<Field>(dojoOld) { new("channel", "string", false) }));
Dojo.Eq("the INC-2290 rename", "breaking: publish a new event version", DeployOrder(dojoOld, new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false), new("amount", "int", false) }));
Dojo.Eq("int widened to long", "consumers first", DeployOrder(dojoOld, new List<Field> { new("orderId", "string", false), new("total", "long", false) }));
record Field(string Name, string Type, bool HasDefault);

steps.title: 3. A Protobuf breaking-change check
prompt: The team's `.proto` contracts get the same gate. A message is described by `Dictionary<int, (string Name, string Type)>`
from field number to field. Write
`List<string> ProtoBreaks(Dictionary<int, (string Name, string Type)> oldFields, Dictionary<int, (string Name, string Type)> newFields, HashSet<int> reserved)`.
Go through the **old** numbers in ascending order:
- number gone from the new message and not in `reserved` → `"field {n} ({name}) removed without reserved"`;
- still there with another type → `"field {n} ({name}) changed type {old} -> {new}"`;
- still there, same type, other name → `"field {n} renamed {old} -> {new}: wire-safe, breaks JSON"`.
Then go through the **new** numbers in ascending order: a number in `reserved` →
`"field {n} ({name}) uses a reserved number"`.
An empty list means the change is safe.
starter: List<string> ProtoBreaks(Dictionary<int, (string Name, string Type)> oldFields, Dictionary<int, (string Name, string Type)> newFields, HashSet<int> reserved)
solution: List<string> ProtoBreaks(Dictionary<int, (string Name, string Type)> oldFields, Dictionary<int, (string Name, string Type)> newFields, HashSet<int> reserved)
else if (f.Type != o.Type) problems.Add($"field {n} ({o.Name}) changed type {o.Type} -> {f.Type}");
else if (f.Name != o.Name) problems.Add($"field {n} renamed {o.Name} -> {f.Name}: wire-safe, breaks JSON");
if (reserved.Contains(n)) problems.Add($"field {n} ({newFields[n].Name}) uses a reserved number");
hints: `oldFields.Keys.OrderBy(k => k)` for the first pass, `newFields.Keys.OrderBy(k => k)` for the second.
`newFields.TryGetValue(n, out var f)` tells you whether the number survived.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoOld = new Dictionary<int, (string Name, string Type)> { [1] = ("order_id", "string"), [2] = ("total_cents", "int64"), [3] = ("currency", "string"), [4] = ("coupon", "string") };
var dojoGood = new Dictionary<int, (string Name, string Type)> { [1] = ("order_id", "string"), [2] = ("total_cents", "int64"), [3] = ("currency", "string"), [5] = ("gift_note", "string") };
Dojo.Eq("remove with reserved, add a new number", new List<string>(), ProtoBreaks(dojoOld, dojoGood, new HashSet<int> { 4 }));
Dojo.Eq("remove without reserved", new List<string> { "field 4 (coupon) removed without reserved" }, ProtoBreaks(dojoOld, dojoGood, new HashSet<int>()));
var dojoBad = new Dictionary<int, (string Name, string Type)> { [1] = ("order_id", "string"), [2] = ("total_cents", "string"), [3] = ("currency_code", "string"), [4] = ("coupon", "string") };

Dojo.Eq("type change and rename", new List<string> { "field 2 (total_cents) changed type int64 -> string", "field 3 renamed currency -> currency_code: wire-safe, breaks JSON" }, ProtoBreaks(dojoOld, dojoBad, new HashSet<int>()));
var dojoReuse = new Dictionary<int, (string Name, string Type)> { [1] = ("order_id", "string"), [2] = ("total_cents", "int64"), [3] = ("currency", "string"), [4] = ("gift_note", "string") };

Dojo.Eq("reusing a reserved number", new List<string> { "field 4 renamed coupon -> gift_note: wire-safe, breaks JSON", "field 4 (gift_note) uses a reserved number" }, ProtoBreaks(dojoOld, dojoReuse, new HashSet<int> { 4 }));

steps.title: 4. Replay the dead letters
prompt: Write `List<string> Replay(IEnumerable<string> parked)` that runs every parked JSON message through a tolerant,
upcasting reader (your `Upcast` is already in the editor) and returns one line per message, in order:
- not valid JSON or not an object → `"park ?: not JSON"`;
- no `orderId` → `"park ?: missing orderId"`;
- `Upcast` throws `NotSupportedException` → `"park {orderId}: {exception message}"`;
- otherwise → `"{orderId} {totalCents} {currency}"` with `currency` defaulting to `"EUR"`.
As before, string values are taken as text and any other value as its raw JSON text. The 3.4 messages used
`amount` (cents) instead of `total`: treat a message that has `amount` and no `total` or `totalCents` as **v2** with
`totalCents = amount` (that is the upcaster for the bad release).
starter: var version = x.TryGetValue("version", out var v) ? int.Parse(v) : 1;
if (version < 1 || version > 3) throw new NotSupportedException($"unknown version {version}");
if (x.Remove("customer", out var customer)) x["customerId"] = customer;
solution: var version = x.TryGetValue("version", out var v) ? int.Parse(v) : 1;
if (version < 1 || version > 3) throw new NotSupportedException($"unknown version {version}");
if (x.Remove("customer", out var customer)) x["customerId"] = customer;
if (doc.RootElement.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.Object) { results.Add("park ?: not JSON"); continue; }
if (!fields.TryGetValue("orderId", out var orderId)) { results.Add("park ?: missing orderId"); continue; }
hints: Parse inside `try { ... } catch (JsonException)` and check for an object before reading properties.
Fix the 3.4 messages before calling `Upcast`: move `amount` to `totalCents` and set `version` to `"2"`.
Catch `NotSupportedException` around `Upcast` and use `ex.Message` in the parked line.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoParked = new[]
"""{"version":3,"orderId":"o-1","amount":1299,"customer":"c-1","giftWrap":true}""",
"""{"version":1,"orderId":"o-2","total":"7.50","customer":"c-2"}""",
"""{"version":3,"orderId":"o-3","totalCents":800,"customerId":"c-3","currency":"SEK"}""",
"""{"version":7,"orderId":"o-4","totalCents":100}""",
"""{"version":3,"totalCents":100}""",
"<html>502 Bad Gateway</html>",
Dojo.Eq("every parked message is replayed or parked with a reason", new List<string>
"park o-4: unknown version 7",
"park ?: missing orderId",
"park ?: not JSON",
"park ?: not JSON",
}, Replay(dojoParked));
Dojo.Eq("nothing parked", new List<string>(), Replay(new string[0]));
